subject: Final close-window: proposed credit structure for Phoenix AI
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Caleb Ross <caleb@phoenix.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@phoenix.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Final close-window: proposed credit structure for Phoenix AI

Hi Caleb / Maya,

Thanks again for the time earlier this week — I know the team is moving fast to finalize procurement before month-end. Based on the usage pattern from the pilot and the outcomes you shared, I put together a couple of close options to make the conversion straightforward for Phoenix AI:

- Option A (Commit+Credit): $250k 12-month commit + $30,000 platform credit applied to first invoice (best unit economics).
- Option B (No commit, extended trial): 60-day trial extension + $20,000 promotional credit applied to usage if you convert within 45 days.
- Option C (Short ramp): 6-month pilot renewed, $15,000 credit, auto-escalate to standard pricing at conversion.

I've attached a short proposal that lays out timing and the minimal T&Cs. If you can confirm the preferred option and procurement timing (are you still aiming for 11/30?), I can route an approval request internally and get a DocuSign addendum over to you.

If helpful, we can also lock a 30-day grace period for invoicing so finance has breathing room.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: phoenix_q4_credit_proposal.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Caleb Ross <caleb@phoenix.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@phoenix.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:18:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Final close-window: proposed credit structure for Phoenix AI

Evelyn — thanks for sending. Helpful framing. A couple quick clarifications:

1) Procurement timeline: we are pushing to sign by 11/30; finance needs the addendum by then to get approval for the commit.
2) Can you share the proposed credit application rules? For instance, do credits reduce invoiced spend dollar-for-dollar in month 1 only, or do they apply across billing cycles until exhausted?
3) Is there flexibility to move some of the credit into a pre-paid bucket rather than a pure invoice rebate?

If we can get Option A or B with a firm addendum by next Monday we can close.

—Caleb
Caleb Ross
Head of Infrastructure | Phoenix AI
caleb@phoenix.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:05:12 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Final close-window: proposed credit structure for Phoenix AI — approval request

Team — forwarding Caleb's questions and the attached proposal. Phoenix is on a hard procurement cadence and wants an addendum by 11/30 to sign. Recommended ask from sales: approve Option A (12m commit + $30k credit) or fallback Option B (60-day extension + $20k credit as a usage rebate) — they prefer Option A but procurement may push for lighter commit.

Key points for approval:
- Credit needs to be escrowed to the first invoice rather than a refund (reduces initial invoice by credit amount).
- If they sign within 45 days, the credit applies dollar-for-dollar across invoices until exhausted; if they never convert, the credit is void (standard).
- If we want to convert some credit to pre-paid balance, ops will need to confirm billing flow.

Attachments: credit_approval_request.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

Can Marcus/Rishi confirm the maximum credit we can offer with no additional approvals? Monica — can you confirm how quickly ops can produce an addendum and whether we can provision a pre-paid bucket if requested?

Thanks — Evelyn

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Final close-window: proposed credit structure for Phoenix AI — approval request

Evelyn — sounds reasonable given ARR potential and strategic fit. Approve up to $30k total promotional credit for PHX-4821 on the condition that:

1) The customer signs and returns the addendum by 11/30.
2) We add a clause limiting credits to usage and explicitly stating credits expire if contract is terminated within first 90 days (protects against churn abuses).
3) Finance (Rishi) to rubber-stamp the accounting treatment; Rishi, please confirm we can treat the $30k as a contra-revenue credit applied to the first two invoices if needed.

Monica — please prepare the addendum template with the above language and provide DocuSign link. If they want a pre-paid bucket instead, ops should create a $20k prepayment SKU and we will honor the reduced billing until it is consumed.

I'm OK with the $30k but prefer the commit (Option A).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Caleb Ross <caleb@phoenix.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@phoenix.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Final close-window: proposed credit structure for Phoenix AI

Caleb / Maya — great news: we can confirm the following, subject to signed addendum by 11/30.

- Offer: $30,000 promotional credit applied to invoices (Option A) if Phoenix signs the 12-month commit by 11/30.
- Fallback: If you prefer no initial commit, we can do a 60-day extension + $20,000 pre-paid credit that will be consumed against usage, valid if you convert within 45 days.

Monica has prepared the addendum and I’ve attached the DocuSign link below. The addendum includes the credit expiration language Marcus requested and the billing treatment. If you can sign by 11/30, we’ll process the credit on your first invoice; if you want pre-paid flow instead we can provision a $20k prepayment SKU within 48 hours of signature.

DocuSign addendum: https://www.docusign.com/secure-sign/PHX-4821-addendum
Attachment: phoenix_q4_credit_proposal.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Please confirm which option you want so I can finalize paperwork. Really appreciate the push here — excited to have Phoenix onboard.

Best,
